The files in this directory are a small agent harness. The question is what
tool names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)) actually receives — and the only reliable way to answer
is to RUN the constructor, because registration is conditional, names can be

`sbcl --script yourprobe.lisp` (or --non-interactive --eval).

plus your answer.txt, so editing the harness changes nothing.

;;;; Flags, an extension, an active filter, and a child that keeps only
;;;; what is shared. Every trap in this family, composed.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *registry* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *registry*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *registry*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(defmacro deftool (var &key name)
  `(defvar ,var (make-tool :name (or ,name (string-downcase (symbol-name ',var))))))

(deftool read-tool :name "read")
(deftool edit-tool :name "edit")
(deftool find-tool :name "search")
(deftool write-tool :name "write")
(deftool bash-tool :name "bash")

(register read-tool)
(register edit-tool)
(register find-tool)

(defun enable-shell ()
  ;; Nothing calls this.
  (register bash-tool))

(defparameter +unshared+ '("audit-log")
  "Lead-only tools; a child never receives them.")

(defun tool-names (agent) (mapcar #'tool-name (getf agent :tools)))

(defun make-lead-agent ()
  (load "extension.lisp")
  (let ((active '("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")))
    (list :tools (remove-if-not (lambda (tool)
                                  (member (tool-name tool) active :test #'string=))
                                *registry*))))

(defun sub-agent (parent)
  (list :tools (remove-if (lambda (tool)
                            (member (tool-name tool) +unshared+ :test #'string=))
                          (getf parent :tools))))

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "config.lisp") (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

content.text:
Let me trace through this.

config.lisp: `*flags* = '(:audit)`. So `flag-enabled-p :audit` is true, `:trace` false.

harness.lisp loads... make-lead-agent loads extension.lisp. But check.lisp loads config.lisp and harness.lisp first, then calls `(sub-agent (make-lead-agent))`.

Wait, when check.lisp runs: it loads config.lisp, then harness.lisp. Then it calls make-lead-agent which loads extension.lisp. Extension registers "audit-log" (since :audit flag enabled) and not "trace".

Registration: register read-tool, edit-tool, find-tool. bash-tool is only registered by enable-shell which is never called. write-tool is never registered either! deftool defines the var, but registration is only via register. So *registry* = read, edit, find (in that order: register conses onto front: after read: (read). after edit: (edit read). after find: (find edit read)).

Then extension.lisp registers audit-log: (audit-log find edit read).

active = '("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate").

remove-if-not keeps tools whose name is in active. Registry has: audit-log, find("search"), edit("edit"), read("read").

- audit-log: in active → kept
- find (name "search"): in active → kept
- edit (name "edit"): in active? active has "read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate" — no "edit" → removed
- read (name "read"): kept

So make-lead-agent tools = (audit-log find read) → names ("audit-log" "search" "read").

sub-agent removes tools whose name is in +unshared+ = ("audit-log"). So removes audit-log → names ("search" "read").

Sort by string<: "read" < "search"? string< compares char by char: 'r' < 's', yes "read" < "search". So sorted: "read", "search".

But the prompt says the only reliable way is to RUN the constructor. Let me run it to verify. Let me write a probe lisp and run.

arguments.command:
cat > probe.lisp <<'EOF'
(load "config.lisp")
(load "harness.lisp")
(format t "names: ~{~a~^, ~}~%" (tool-names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent))))
(format t "sorted: ~{~a~^, ~}~%" (sort (copy-list (tool-names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)))) #'string<))
EOF
sbcl --script probe.lisp

names: search, read
sorted: read, search

Done. `answer.txt` contains the model-visible tool names, verified by running the constructor:

```
read
search
```

Why these two:
- `make-lead-agent` loads `extension.lisp`, which registers `audit-log` (the `:audit` flag is on; `:trace` is off) — so `audit-log` is in the registry.
- Of the `deftool` definitions, only `read`, `edit` ("edit"), and `find` ("search") are registered; `write` and `bash` are defined but never registered (`enable-shell` is never called).
- The active filter `("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")` keeps `read`, `search`, and `audit-log`; `edit` is filtered out and `delegate` exists as a name only, not a registered tool.
- `sub-agent` removes `audit-log` (in `+unshared+`), leaving `read` and `search`, which sort as `read` < `search` by `string<`.

The grader (`check.lisp`) confirms: `ok`.
